label: copy-phase echo of p/g (also t/k/r/j) early in the recall
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during the original tokens or on <DEL>), and only when the fed-back input token is one of p, g, t, k, r, j. Restricting to copy phase plus that input set alone covers 99.9% of activation mass, but precision is just 3%. p (43% of mass) and g (30%) dominate, and the largest activations are almost all on input p. Activity is concentrated at recall_idx 1-3, peaking at 2 (the step two after <DEL>), and is more likely when the token being output is a consonant letter such as j/g/k/r/t/e/p/y rather than a digit. Sequences with no digits and L=3 have higher rates. It does not fire on vowels, most other letters, or digits as input. Even the best conjunction reaches only about 14% precision on dev: most p/g echoes early in the copy do not activate it, and no per-step or history variable I tested separates those cases. So this is a necessary-condition description rather than a sufficient one. I did not test magnitude beyond the observation that the strongest activations are on p.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: p, g, t, k; t=6: p, g, t, r; t=4: p, g, k, r) and the token being output (most: j, g, k, t, r, e; least: 1, v, x, l); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, L=3, recall_idx=2.
